name: Vespers Ninefold

detectability.signature: Nine concentric chroniton rings emitting an identical repeating burst pattern every 6.2 hours, phase-locked across all nine

proximity: Crew experience déjà vu of events that have not yet occurred in the current cycle
Shipboard systems begin replaying logged telemetry from the previous iteration
contact: Vessels crossing the innermost ring are reset to the loop's beginning with memories intact but records erased
Physical damage sustained inside the ring persists only until the next reset
prolonged_exposure: Trapped in time loop, reliving the same 6.2 hours indefinitely while retaining full awareness
Memory loss or temporal disorientation as accumulated iterations blur which events belong to which cycle
Equipment malfunction from timeline interference as components carry wear from hundreds of resets

phenomena: Visible echoes of past events repeating identically at fixed points in each cycle
Radio signals arriving before being sent, always exactly one loop ahead
Objects existing in multiple timeframes simultaneously at the ring boundaries
hazards: Trapped in time loop with no confirmed method of exit
Memory loss or temporal disorientation after many iterations
opportunities: Perfect rehearsal environment: any attempt can be repeated endlessly until it succeeds
Archaeological significance as the only surviving megastructure of the Vesperine Concordance
Recovery of lost ships/personnel stranded within the loop's memory banks
known_incidents: The tug Anvil Song spent what its crew counted as eleven years inside the loop; external sensors recorded a single afternoon, and the crew emerged fluent in a dead language they had learned from loop echoes
A daredevil racing circuit attempted to use the reset for unlimited practice runs; the fourth iteration ended when pilots could no longer remember which lap had killed them
description: Nine rings of pale violet light hang nested around a common center like the layers of a clockwork rose, each precisely eighty-five kilometers across and each pulsing in perfect unison. The structure is unmistakably made: geometry this exact does not occur in nature, and faint structural spars are visible at the rings' cardinal points. Every 6.2 hours, all nine rings flare together and everything within begins again.

The loop is absolute and mercifully regular. Anything inside the innermost ring at the moment of reset returns to the cycle's first second, carrying memories forward but wounds backward; hulls emerge pristine no matter what burned within them. Signals transmitted from inside arrive outside one full loop before they are sent, letting observers receive tomorrow's traffic today. Veterans navigate by the echoes, since every event inside repeats identically.

The Vesperine Concordance built the rings some nine centuries ago for purposes still debated, though the prevailing theory holds it was a rehearsal engine for events too dangerous to attempt once. The tug Anvil Song proved the loop's strangest property: her crew lived eleven subjective years inside a single recorded afternoon, emerging speaking a language dead for eight hundred years. The Concordance left no manuals, only the rings and their patient chime.

Today the loop is fenced by treaty buoys and visited by two kinds of travelers: scholars reading the Concordance's echoes, and desperate people who need infinite attempts at something. Exit is possible, the Anvil Song proves it, but no one has explained why some resets release and others do not. Enter knowing the cost is measured not in hours but in how many times you can stand to live the same one.
